description: The N>>500 route: run one SQL statement against a registered foreign Postgres connection and write the result as ONE tab-separated .tsv file at an ABSOLUTE output_tsv_path in the operator's workspace. Returns immediately with a job_id and status 'queued' (D0.3 deferred-completion shape) — the dispatch returning is NOT the same as the job finishing; the written path, columns, row_count, and truncated flag are delivered when the job completes. The path must lie under a saved location (the installation tree is always excluded). Same commit-after-write behaviour and override mechanism as run_query, with a higher hard cap: this connection targets an arbitrary customer database, so there is no vendor-imposed row ceiling, only our own policy. Defaults to 500 rows absent an acknowledged override -- for that common small/default case, run_query has an identical interface with a lower ceiling. To fetch more, pass acknowledge_default_limit_override=true together with an explicit row_limit (up to 50000) -- both are required together, and a row_limit above 50000 is refused rather than silently clamped. Requires connection_name, sql, and output_tsv_path. When the goal is validating that records exist rather than inspecting their content, prefer selecting stable ID columns over email addresses or other PII-bearing fields — the query decides what columns land in the file.
embedding_description: Export a BULK query result -- up to 50,000 rows with an acknowledged override -- to a workspace TSV, for pulls too large for run_query's lower ceiling. Dispatches asynchronously, returning a job_id while the high-volume file is assembled in the background, taking noticeably longer than the everyday query surface. Prefer stable ID columns over PII fields.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dispatch envelope: job_id (string) and status ('queued'). This is NOT the export result — the TSV handle (path, columns, row_count, truncated) arrives separately when the job completes and is delivered as its own message.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call only confirms the job was queued — do not present job_id/status as the export result. Acknowledge the request is in flight; the TSV handle lands in a follow-up message when the job completes. Once delivered, confirm the export: the written path, the row_count, and the column list. The file contains potentially sensitive corporate database content -- name the path for downstream use (open it, feed it to create_spreadsheet_from_files, join it with other exports) but do not inline its contents. If truncated is true, warn that the export hit the effective limit and point to a higher acknowledged row_limit (up to 50000) if more is needed.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Export one statement's result from a registered foreign Postgres connection to a tab-separated file in the operator's workspace, up to an acknowledged override ceiling.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: external_pg.invalid_params: missing connection_name/sql/output_tsv_path, the path's parent directory does not exist, acknowledge_default_limit_override and row_limit were not given together, or row_limit exceeded the 50000 hard cap. external_pg.export_path_refused: the path must be absolute, have the required suffix where specified, and lie under a saved path address, the session folder or solet home, outside the installation tree. Input files must already exist. external_pg.connection_unknown: no connection registered under that name. external_pg.read_only_sql_transaction: the SERVER refused a write because the transaction is read-only there (a hot standby, or the role's default_transaction_read_only setting).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: external_pg.invalid_params naming the override pair: pass BOTH acknowledge_default_limit_override=true and an explicit row_limit, or neither (for the 500-row default); a row_limit above 50000 is refused outright, not clamped. external_pg.export_path_refused: ask "where will you save this?" and use the returned folder, or say "save exports for <project> in <folder>" to save a project location. Keep it outside the installation tree; input files must already exist. external_pg.connection_unknown: run list_connections. external_pg.read_only_sql_transaction: point the write at a primary server or a role whose default_transaction_read_only is off.
